# FLX-3505: a sink could not finish writing a stream

**Family:** seam/conformance (the 3000 band)

The destination refused a write part-way: a disk filled up, a permission was missing, a file could not be renamed into place, an object store could not be set up or refused an upload, or a read-back check found data that does not digest to the stream's outputDigest. A file sink writing to a local directory stages every file under a hidden name and renames it into place only when the whole stream is written, and it removes what it staged when it fails, so no partial stream is left for a reader to mistake for a whole one. On an object store the manifest is uploaded last and a stream is whole only when its manifest object is there; when an upload fails, the data objects this delivery had written are deleted, best effort and by their exact keys, and the message says whether that worked and which keys remain if not. Nothing is deleted when the manifest of an earlier, complete delivery of the stream is already in place, because the new objects have the same names and bytes. The objects are also kept when the manifest of the stream is in place after the failure, or when whether it is there cannot be checked, for example because the credential may not read it. An endpoint that does not answer is retried for up to 3 minutes, obstore's default, before the failure; to give up sooner pass --sink-opt retry-timeout=SECONDS (and max-retries=N, request-timeout=SECONDS or connect-timeout=SECONDS, for the parquet and arrow-ipc sinks). When a delivery to several streams fails part-way, the message names the stream that failed and says how many streams were delivered; their receipts are kept in sink-receipts.json and the later streams were not attempted. An object store failure that comes of the credentials or the endpoint ends with the settings to check: the AWS_* variables and AWS_ALLOW_HTTP for s3://, GOOGLE_* for gs://, AZURE_* for az:// and abfs://. The message names variables, never their values. An object store target with no credential in the environment is refused before the run, with nothing contacted, because the store would otherwise ask the cloud's instance metadata service (169.254.169.254 and its siblings) for one; to use the credentials of the machine or workload the run is on (an instance role, a pod or managed identity), pass --sink-opt instance-identity=true. Whatever the target, the run directory and its outputDigest are unaffected and the run is kept: after the cause is fixed, publish it again with fluxsim apply BUNDLE --run-id RUN_ID --sink TARGET (the command prints it, with --state-dir when one was given), which writes the same files under the same names.
